items.msg: modal pad size (1.9, 3.7) mm != datasheet (1.4, 3.7) mm (tol 0.1)

land_pattern.package: CKCS4030 - from the datasheet's 'Recommended patterns' drawing (F/G/H, Fig 2 sheet) and the CKCS4030 row of the SHAPES AND DIMENSIONS table.
land_pattern.notes: RECOMMENDED PATTERN (CKCS4030 row, mm): F = 1.2 (gap between the two pads), G = 1.40 (pad width, along the 4.0 mm body axis that carries the electrodes), H = 3.7 (pad length, across the body). The 'Recommended patterns' figure dimensions F between the facing pad edges, G across one pad, H down one pad. DERIVED pad-centre spacing = F + G = 1.2 + 1.40 = 2.60 mm (this is pitch_mm); overall land span = G + F + G = 4.00 mm, exactly the body width A. BODY (CKCS4030 row): A = 4.0 +/-0.2 (width), B = 4.0 +/-0.2 (depth), C = 3.0 Max (height), D = 1.3 +/-0.3 (gap between the bottom electrodes), E = 1.35 +/-0.3 (each bottom electrode width); body style Fig 3. CROSS-CHECK / CONFLICT (not a datasheet statement): KiCad 10.0 ships Inductor_SMD:L_Cenker_CKCS4030 with pads at x = +/-1.35 sized 1.9 x 3.7 - i.e. pad-centre spacing 2.70 mm and pad width 1.9 mm, versus this datasheet's 2.60 mm and 1.40 mm. The pad LENGTH (3.7 mm) agrees. Consequence: running fp_verify against that library footprint with this JSON will report a pad_pitch ERROR (2.70 measured vs 2.60 expected, 0.10 > the 0.05 mm default tolerance) and a pad_size WARNING (1.9 vs 1.4). Both lands are physically usable - KiCad's is the more generous one, extending 0.30 mm further outboard and 0.20 mm further inboard - but a decision is needed: either accept the library footprint and relax the tolerance, or generate the land from this datasheet. This is a real library-vs-datasheet divergence, not an extraction error.
